title.narrative: Support Food Security and Agriculture at Sweida

description.narrative: ltpgtThe residents of the villages of Malah (southern countryside) and Mshannaf (eastern countryside) in As-Suwayda rely heavily on agriculture, livestock, and poultry farming as primary sources of livelihoodltbrgtDuring the Syrian crisis, the region's water, agriculture, livestock sectors, and infrastructure were significantly damaged. Climate changes further exacerbated the decline in agricultural production, adversely affecting the living and social conditions of families, including internally displaced persons and the local communityltbrgtBACC, after coordination with authorized government through the Agriculture and Livestock Program, aims to improve the livelihoods of those still at risk in affected areas, helping them find decent livelihoods and supporting them in obtaining more work. This is closely linked to investing in natural resources. BACC worked for 4 years to distribute livestock grants include: chicken, feed, Barley seeds , medicines vitamin.lt/pgtltpgtRequired approvals: ministry of agriculture sub-relief committeeltbrgtThe food and agricultural security project planned by BACC aims to support 1000 families selected from those working in agriculture, livestock, and poultry to achieve self-sufficiency and face winter-related risksltbrgtProject ImportanceltbrgtRegion Selection Criteria: project relies on the specialized criteria of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, alongside assessments and priority rankingsltbrgtImproving Food Security: Chickens are a crucial source of animal protein, providing both meat and eggs. Eggs and chicken meat are lower in fat compared to other protein sources, making them a healthier choice for many peopleltbrgtEconomic Sector Improvement: The poultry sector creates direct and indirect job opportunities in farms, factories, transportation, and marketing companies. It enhances rural job opportunities and reduces migration to cities, encouraging small business startups through entrepreneurship courses and promoting loans to open supplementary projects to poultry farmingltbrgtSustainability: The project ensures the purchase of chickens from government farms, guaranteeing all necessary vaccinations and veterinary checks. The project also aims to train beneficiaries on new mechanisms and techniques to maintain chicken health and increase productivity through training on climate change adaptation techniques—such as administering medications, vitamins, and minerals awareness about common diseases designing housing with adequate humidity, ventilation, and lighting waste management and reuse for biogas production or as fertilizer, which is rich in soil-supporting elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and calcium, and environmentally friendlyltbrgtComprehensive Support: The project will supply all necessary production requirements in appropriate quantities and forms suitable for agricultural work, climatic changes, and temperature drops. All interventions will consider factors like land area, environmental conditions, available workforce, and the ability to use modern adaptation mechanisms and techniquesltbrgtEnvironmental Protection: Environmental protection will be considered, ensuring that project activities do not support any environmentally harmful practices. The sustainable project plan seeks eco-friendly adaptation mechanisms by using animal waste as fertilizers instead of chemicals. In the long run, the project includes plans to use these wastes for natural gas fermentation, producing one cubic meter of natural gas from every three tons of chicken waste, with each chicken producing about 100-150 grams of waste daily.ltbrgtThese interventions will be implemented based on our approachesltbrgtAGDltbrgtPSEAltbrgtCommunity-based approachltbrgtHumanity, Neutrality, Impartiality, and Independence ApproachltbrgtCommunity participationltbrgtCommunity accountabilityltbrgtSelection criterialtbrgtMost vulnerable familiesltbrgtReturnee families ltbrgtWomen who head families ltbrgtFamilies that include PWDsltbrgtFamilies include elderly ltbrgtFamilies at risk of protectionlt/pgt
